text:
nate: quick PSA: onboarding sample failed in a Next Edge preview after I updated package exports. Works in Node but edge throws syntax errors.

ashish: paste error and package.json?

nate: error: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'` during vercel build. package.json snippet:
```json
{ "name": "@redwood/sdk", "version": "0.4.1", "main": "cjs/index.cjs.js", "module": "esm/index.mjs", "exports": { ".": { "import": "esm/index.mjs", "require": "cjs/index.cjs.js" } }, "types": "types/index.d.ts" }
```

rina: SWC + edge bundlers treat .mjs as native ESM and sometimes pass it through. If we shipped modern syntax (top-level await / export maps) that the edge shim doesn’t support, it breaks. Also tsc in workspaces can misresolve types if `exports` doesn’t include type paths.

kevin: saw similar customer report. They upgraded and only edge functions failed. Server (node) was fine.

ashish: short-term: remove `module` or point it to a transpiled esm (.js) bundle; or ship a safer ESM that avoids bleeding-edge syntax. For types: mirror declarations alongside each export or include `exports."./types"` so tsc can find them.

nate: confirmed: deleting `module` locally fixed the vercel preview.

rina: long-term: publish a normalized exports map during build that includes `import`/`require`/`types` entries and a default fallback. Add a CI smoke test: fresh Next + edge install of the tarball.

ashish: opening a patch PR and issue now. will add changelog note and rollback guidance.

devx-bot: Issue created: redwood-inference/sdk#2367 "exports/esm release causing Edge/TS resolution issues" (assigned: ashish)

kevin: thanks — please fast-track patch, customers impacted in prod.
